_note: DRAFT starter table written from general pharmacology knowledge. Every entry has reviewed=false. Verify each against a trusted reference (BNF, Stockley's, Micromedex, the product label) and only then set reviewed=true and fill 'source'. This table is the rules engine: the LLM may explain it but must never override it. Drug names must match generic_name in drugs.py.

interactions.effect: Increased risk of bleeding (additive anticoagulant and antiplatelet effects; aspirin can also injure GI mucosa).
interactions.management: Avoid unless specifically indicated; if combined, monitor INR and watch for bleeding.

interactions.effect: Increased bleeding risk (NSAID antiplatelet effect and GI injury on top of anticoagulation).
interactions.management: Avoid where possible; consider paracetamol for pain; monitor INR and bleeding if unavoidable.

interactions.effect: May raise INR and increase bleeding risk.
interactions.management: Monitor INR closely when starting or stopping the antibiotic.

interactions.effect: Increased INR and bleeding have been reported.
interactions.management: Monitor INR during and after the antibiotic course.

interactions.effect: Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C9 and raises warfarin exposure, increasing INR and bleeding risk.
interactions.management: Monitor INR closely; warfarin dose reduction is often needed.

interactions.effect: Thyroid hormone can increase the anticoagulant effect of warfarin.
interactions.management: Monitor INR when starting, stopping or changing levothyroxine dose.

interactions.effect: Correcting hyperthyroidism can reduce warfarin sensitivity (and the reverse when stopping), changing INR.
interactions.management: Monitor INR as thyroid status changes.

interactions.effect: Increased bleeding risk (SSRI effect on platelets; possible CYP2C9 inhibition raising warfarin levels).
interactions.management: Monitor INR and bleeding.

interactions.effect: Increased bleeding risk (SSRI effect on platelets).

interactions.effect: Pantoprazole has weaker CYP2C19 inhibition than omeprazole, so less effect on clopidogrel activation.
interactions.management: Generally the preferred PPI with clopidogrel; confirm with current label.

interactions.effect: Additive bleeding risk. Often an intentional combination (dual antiplatelet therapy).
interactions.management: Use only when indicated; monitor for bleeding.

interactions.effect: Ibuprofen can interfere with the antiplatelet effect of low-dose aspirin; additive GI bleeding risk.
interactions.management: If both are needed, take aspirin first and separate the doses; consider alternatives.

interactions.effect: Therapeutic duplication (two angiotensin receptor blockers): hypotension, hyperkalaemia, renal impairment.
interactions.management: Do not combine; clarify the prescription with the prescriber.

interactions.effect: Dual renin-angiotensin blockade: hyperkalaemia, hypotension, renal impairment.
interactions.management: Generally avoid; monitor potassium and renal function if ever used.

interactions.management: Monitor heart rate and blood pressure; dose adjustment may be needed.

interactions.effect: Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6 and raises tricyclic levels; additive serotonergic effect (serotonin syndrome) and QT/anticholinergic toxicity.
interactions.management: Avoid or use lower tricyclic doses with monitoring.

interactions.effect: Sertraline may raise tricyclic levels; additive serotonergic effect.
interactions.management: Monitor for toxicity and serotonin syndrome.

interactions.effect: Itraconazole is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor and greatly raises alprazolam levels (profound sedation). Check the alprazolam label for this contraindication.
interactions.management: Do not co-administer; choose an alternative.

interactions.effect: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition raises atorvastatin exposure: risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
interactions.management: Avoid or limit the statin dose per the label; consider a statin not metabolised by CYP3A4.

interactions.effect: Moderate CYP3A4 inhibition may raise atorvastatin levels, increasing the risk of muscle toxicity.
interactions.management: Monitor for muscle pain or weakness; consider temporary statin hold or dose reduction.

interactions.effect: Reduced gastric acid can reduce levothyroxine absorption.
interactions.management: Monitor TSH when starting or stopping the PPI; adjust levothyroxine dose if needed.
